findings.title: getCalendarCredentials stores un-awaited promises in the result
findings.body: getCalendar is now async, so `calendar` in each returned item is a Promise<Calendar|null>. Only getConnectedCalendars awaits it. Other callers of getCalendarCredentials that use `.calendar` directly (for example the availability code) will now get a Promise and fail or silently misbehave. The inferred type of the `calendar` field changed with no compile-time check at those call sites. The calendar should be resolved before it is returned, or every consumer must be audited.

findings.title: async forEach callback makes errors unhandled and un-awaited
findings.body: Converting the forEach callback to async means the returned promises are never awaited. The surrounding try/catch cannot catch rejections from getCalendar or deleteEvent, so a failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Reschedule continues and returns before calendar and video deletions finish, which is risky in serverless runtimes. The same pattern is repeated in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts and in trpc bookings.tsx requestReschedule. Use `await Promise.all(refs.map(...))` instead.

findings.title: async forEach pushes to apiDeletes after it has been awaited
findings.body: The recurring-cancel branch uses `forEach(async ...)`. It now awaits getCalendar before it reaches the loop that pushes into apiDeletes. Because forEach does not wait, `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs while apiDeletes is still empty. The calendar deletions for recurring bookings are therefore not awaited, can be dropped, and may reject unhandled. Previously the callback ran synchronously up to the first await. Use a for...of loop.

findings.title: Dynamic imports are started eagerly at module load
findings.body: Every `import(...)` in the appStore object literal runs when the module is first imported. All 29 apps are loaded immediately, so this is not lazy loading. Any failing app import becomes an unhandled rejection at startup. Making each entry a function such as `() => import(...)` would give real lazy loading.
